title: 1994 Mull of Kintyre Chinook crash
summary: RAF Chinook ZD576 flew into a hillside in dense fog on 2 June 1994. Around 18:00 Chinook crashed into terrain on Mull of Kintyre in foggy conditions. The helicopter was carrying 25 British intelligence experts from MI5 and other agencies. All twenty-five passengers and four crew on board were killed, making it the RAF's fourth-worst peacetime disaster.
probable_cause: Controlled flight into terrain in instrument meteorological conditions. Initial 1995 board ruled cause impossible to establish. Reviewing officers stated pilots flew too fast and too low in thick fog. 2011 independent review cleared crew of negligence and found RAF falsely declared compliance with aircraft authority to fly.

factors.evidence: weather forecast was clear except in Mull of Kintyre area; aircraft flew into a hillside in dense fog
technical issues surrounding the then-new Chinook HC2 variant were uncovered; technical problems with specific airframe in weeks leading to crash
RAF had falsely declared compliance with regulations in relation to aircraft authority to fly
Chinook ZD576 flew into a hillside in dense fog around 18:00
